extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants, recipients, program officials, grants management staff, and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitional requirements from the NIH Grants Policy Statement covering terms and substantive policy requirements (e.g., allowable costs, clinical trial definitions, data and safety monitoring, consortium agreements, carryover rules) used by applicants and recipients to prepare, manage, and comply with NIH awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable cost
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost incurred by a recipient that is: (1) reasonable for the performance of the award; (2) allocable; (3) in conformance with any limitations or exclusions set forth in the Federal cost principles applicable to the organization incurring the cost or in the NoA as to the type or amount of cost; (4) consistent with regulations, policies, and procedures of the recipient that are applied uniformly to both federally supported and other activities of the organization; (5) accorded consistent treatment as a direct or indirect cost; (6) determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles; and (7) not included as a cost in any other federally supported award (unless specifically authorized by statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional information on each, see Cost Considerations—The Cost Principles. The Allowable cost definition ties allowability to reasonableness, allocability, conformity to cost principles and Notice of Award (NoA) limits, consistent internal practices, GAAP, and no double-charging across awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for (or the award of) additional funds during a current project period to provide for an increase in costs due to unforeseen circumstances. All additional costs must be within the current scope of the peer reviewed and approved project. Administrative supplements do not require peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative supplements must remain within the approved project scope; they are intended to address unforeseen cost increases and typically do not undergo peer review (contrast with competitive revisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration and renovation (A&R) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Alteration and renovation activities are considered modernization activities and are typically supported under research grants where the primary purpose for the grant is other than construction or modernization. The determination of whether proposed A&R is major or minor is made by the NIH Program Official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether A&R is allowable and whether it is classified as major or minor rests with the NIH Program Official; see the Modernization and Construction chapters for additional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Welfare Assurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Animal Welfare Assurance is part of the required documentation to receive an award for organizations involved in live, vertebrate animal activity conducted or supported by the Public Health Service (PHS). The Animal Welfare Assurance enumerates the organization’s commitment to compliance with the PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and other incorporated laws and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations conducting vertebrate animal research must have an Animal Welfare Assurance on file as part of required award documentation; the Assurance documents institutional commitments to applicable PHS and regulatory animal care requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable clinical trial (FDAAA) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Applicable clinical trial’ is the term used in Title VIII of the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act (FDAAA) of 2007 (P.L. 110-85) to designate the scope of clinical trials that may be subject to the registration and results reporting requirements in FDAAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FDAAA criteria to determine which clinical trials are subject to statutory registration and results reporting obligations; consult FDAAA and related guidance for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for financial support of a project or activity submitted to NIH on specified forms and in accordance with NIH instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the forms and follow the instructions specified in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and application guidance. See Application Information and Processes for details about application types, forms, and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover of unobligated funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Unobligated Federal funds remaining at the end of any budget period that, with the approval of the Grants Management Officer (GMO) or under an automatic authority, may be carried forward to another budget period to cover allowable costs of that budget period. Obligated, but unliquidated, funds are not considered carryover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must obtain GMO approval or rely on an applicable automatic carryover authority to transfer unobligated Federal funds between budget periods; understand distinction between unobligated and obligated-but-unliquidated funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in scope (prior approval requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity whereby the objectives or specific aims identified in the approved grant application are significantly changed by the recipient after award. GMO prior approval is required for a change in scope to be allowable under an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant changes to aims or objectives after award require prior approval from the GMO; see Administrative Requirements—Changes in Project and Budget—Prior Approval Requirements—Change of Scope for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of PD/PI
rubrics_metrics.description: A process, usually initiated by the recipient, whereby the federally approved PD/PI is replaced by another individual, with the approval of the GMO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement of the PD/PI requires submission to and approval by the GMO and must follow NIH multiple-PI and PD/PI change policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium agreement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A formalized agreement whereby a research project is carried out by the recipient and one or more other organizations that are separate legal entities. Under the agreement, the recipient must perform a substantive role in the conduct of the planned research and not merely serve as a conduit of funds to another party or parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium agreements typically involve a specific level of effort from the collaborating organization's PD/PI and a categorical breakdown of costs (personnel, supplies, indirect costs). Such relationships are considered subawards; see Consortium Agreements chapter for required content and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing personal interest that could affect, or could appear to affect, an individual’s judgment or could cause the individual’s impartiality to be questioned. Conflicts of Interest (actual or potential) may arise in the objective review process or in other activities and phases of the financial assistance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term is cross-cutting across peer review, financial conflict of interest, and responsible conduct of research policies. See Financial Conflict of Interest and other relevant chapters for specific rules and disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost principles applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The government-wide principles established under 2 CFR Part 200 for determining the allowable costs incurred by non-Federal entities under Federal awards. The principles are for the purpose of cost determination and are not intended to identify the circumstances or dictate the extent of Federal Government participation in financing of a particular program or project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs must be determined in accordance with 2 CFR Part 200; hospitals follow Appendix IX; for-profit organizations follow FAR (48 CFR Part 31.2). See Cost Considerations—The Cost Principles for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing / matching
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of project costs not paid by Federal funds or contributions (unless authorized by Federal statute). This term includes matching, which refers to required levels of cost share that must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost sharing obligations must conform to 2 CFR Part 200.306 and the NOFO; documented and auditable records must support any cost share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical research is research with human subjects that includes: (1) patient-oriented research (direct interaction with human subjects or on material of human origin that can be linked to a living individual); (2) epidemiological and behavioral studies; (3) outcomes research and health services research. Studies falling under certain regulatory exemptions (e.g., 45 CFR Part 46 exemptions such as pre-2018 or Revised Common Rule Exemption 4) are not considered clinical research by this definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of whether an activity is clinical research affects applicable policy requirements (human subjects protections, IRB review, data requirements). Consult applicable Common Rule citations provided for specifics about exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial definition and components
rubrics_metrics.description: A research study in which one or more human subjects are prospectively assigned to one or more interventions (which may include placebo or other control) to evaluate the effects of those interventions on health-related biomedical or behavioral outcomes. 'Prospectively assigned' refers to a pre-defined process (e.g., randomization). An intervention includes manipulation of the subject or the subject’s environment (drugs, biologics, devices, procedures, delivery systems, behavioral strategies). A health-related outcome is the pre-specified effect of an intervention (physiological, psychological, disease processes, behavior, quality of life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical trials may be categorized by phases: Phase I (first-in-human small safety/efficacy), Phase II (larger efficacy and safety), Phase III (large comparative efficacy and safety, collect info for safe use), Phase IV (post-marketing surveillance). The definition cross-references Common Rule citations for research and human subject definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and safety monitoring plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each NIH-supported clinical trial, NIH requires a data and safety monitoring plan that will provide oversight and monitoring to ensure the safety of participants and the validity and integrity of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The level of monitoring should be commensurate with the risks and the size and complexity of the clinical trial. A detailed data and safety monitoring plan must be submitted to the applicant’s IRB and subsequently to the awarding IC for approval prior to the accrual of human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Data Management & Sharing Plan (DMS Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Management: the process of validating, organizing, protecting, maintaining, and processing scientific data to ensure the accessibility, reliability, and quality of the scientific data for its users. Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMS Plan): a plan describing the data management, preservation, and sharing of scientific data and accompanying metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must prepare DMS Plans as required by NIH policies (describe management, preservation, sharing, and associated metadata). The DMS Plan informs expectations for data stewardship and repository deposit where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Sharing (policy principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of making scientific data available for use by others (e.g., the larger research community, institutions, the broader public), for example, via an established repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data sharing is encouraged/required per NIH policy; the DMS Plan should specify how and where data will be shared and any applicable protections for privacy or confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and suspension standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions taken by a debarring official in accordance with OMB guidance at 2 CFR Part 180, as implemented by HHS in 2 CFR Part 376, to exclude a person or organization from participating in grants and other non-procurement awards government-wide. If debarred or suspended, the person or organization may not receive financial assistance for a specified period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debarment/suspension under 2 CFR Part 376 are distinct from post-award suspension actions by an awarding agency. See Public Policy Requirements and Objectives—Debarment and Suspension for procedures and impacts.
